shapes.name: TextBox 9
shapes.text:
Problem Statement ID – SIH26181
Problem Statement Title- A secure, AI-powered Personal Health Companion that delivers real-time, privacy-preserving health monitoring and early warning capabilities, helping individuals recognize health risks before they become emergencies. The solution should improve resilience during heat waves, floods, pollution events, and other disasters common in India while enabling continuous health support through on-device intelligence.
Theme- MedTech / BioTech / HealthTech
PS Category- Hardware
Team Name- IgniteX

shapes.name: TextBox 1
shapes.text:
Detailed explanation of the proposed solution
Athena is a wearable health-monitoring device with a hybrid edge-cloud AI architecture
Sensors (MAX30102, body temp, BME280, MPU6050) feed a fused risk score computed on-device via TinyML
When connected, Google Gemini provides deeper AI health advisory; the system runs fully offline otherwise
How it addresses the problem
Continuously monitors HR, SpO2, body temp, and motion — matches the PS's core monitoring requirement
Detects heat-stress and fall risk in real time using on-device inference, even with no internet [1]
GSM-based SOS to caregivers works independent of WiFi — solving the exact "disaster connectivity loss" gap in the problem statement
Innovation and uniqueness of the solution
Hybrid offline (TinyML) / online (Gemini) intelligence — most competitors assume constant connectivity
Live 3D motion-telemetry visualization (wireframe avatar reflecting real movement/fall state)
Tiered, escalating alert system (vibration → OLED → full SOS) instead of a single binary alarm

shapes.name: TextBox 8
shapes.text:
Technologies to be used
ESP32 (edge compute) + MAX30102, BME280, MPU6050 sensors, OLED display, vibration motor, GSM module
TinyML for on-device inference, Google Gemini 2.5 API for cloud-side advisory
MQTT (HiveMQ) → Docker backend → Render hosting → WebSocket live dashboard
Three.js for real-time 3D motion-telemetry visualization

Methodology and process for implementation
Pipeline: Sensors → local risk fusion (TinyML) → MQTT publish → dashboard + Gemini analysis (if online) → SOS alert

shapes.name: TextBox 8
shapes.text:
Analysis of the feasibility of the idea
All components are off-the-shelf and already integrated in a working prototype, not just a concept
Potential challenges and risks
Network dependency for Gemini advisory
Wearable battery life under continuous sensing
Sensor accuracy/placement (body temp, HR) needs calibration
Strategies for overcoming these challenges
TinyML offline fallback removes dependency on constant connectivity
Deep-sleep duty cycling extends battery life
GSM module ensures SOS works with zero WiFi/internet
Debounce logic (sustained risk threshold) prevents false-alarm SOS triggers

shapes.name: TextBox 8
shapes.text:
Potential impact on the target audience
Elderly, outdoor laborers, rural/disaster-prone populations, and chronic-condition patients — directly matching the PS's stated vulnerable groups [2]

Benefits of the solution (social, economic, environmental)
Social: Early warning before emergencies; functions without connectivity during the exact disasters that knock out other systems [3]
Economic: Low-cost, decentralized monitoring vs. clinical-grade devices
Environmental: Edge-first processing reduces continuous cloud data transmission and associated energy use

shapes.name: TextBox 8
shapes.text:
[1] WHO — Heat and Healthwho.int→ Grounds the heat-stress detection use case in documented public health risk.
[2] NDMA — Heat Wave Guidelines, Government of Indiandma.gov.in→ Supports the "resilience during heat waves/disasters" claim directly from the problem statement.
[3] Ayushman Bharat Digital Missionabdm.gov.in→ Aligns Athena with India's existing push toward accessible, low-cost digital healthcare.
[4] Existing wearables — Fitbit, Apple Watch, Google Fit (comparative note)→ These assume constant connectivity for meaningful health insights; none are built for offline-first operation during disasters — this is the gap Athena addresses.
[5] Athena — Live Project Dashboard[https://athena-ai-13ci.onrender.com/→ Working prototype, publicly viewable.
